questions.question_text:
Decomposition is a type of reaction in which a single compound
splits into two or more simple compounds. Decomposition
reactions are generally classified into three types, depending
upon the type of energy required for the reaction. The three
types are thermal decomposition, photolytic decomposition and
electrolytic decomposition.
(a) Why are decomposition reactions known as endothermic
reactions ?
(b) Give an example of photolytic decomposition.
(c) Name the gas liberated at the (i) cathode, and (ii) anode
when water is electrolysed. Write the molar ratio of
hydrogen and oxygen (Hydrogen : Oxygen) liberated
during electrolysis.
OR
(c) What happens when lead nitrate powder is heated in a
boiling tube ? Write chemical equation for the reaction.

marking_points.point: (a) • due to absorption of heat.

(b) • In the presence of sunlight, silver bromide (AgBr) decomposes into
silver (Ag) metal and bromine (Br2) / 2AgBr → 2Ag + Br2 ℎν
( or any other example)
(c) • Gas liberated at cathode – hydrogen (H2)
• Gas liberated at anode – oxygen (O2)

• Molar ratio of hydrogen and oxygen liberated on electrolysis of
water is 2 : 1
OR
c) • Brown fumes are produced / Decomposition

• 2Pb(NO3)2 ⎯heat ⎯ ⎯ ⎯ → 2PbO + 4 NO2 +O2
[Note: Do not cut marks if equation is not balanced]
